subject: Renewal options for API gateway / WAF / CDN (Cloudflare renewal + Akamai/Fastly evaluation)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, procurement@vendorops.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cloudflare renewal — need options + risk notes

Hi team,

Quick heads up — Cloudflare sent the enterprise renewal for our edge stack (WAF + CDN + API Gateway) and the numbers are up ~22% on list compared to last year. Attached is the quote (CF_enterprise_quote_Q4_2025.pdf).

We need to decide whether to:
- Accept Cloudflare renewal (negotiate term/discount/SLA), or
- Move to Akamai (term sheet attached from Ruben) or
- Run a narrow Fastly PoC for our high-RPS APIs and evaluate cost/latency.

Key constraints:
- Security: WAF rules and SOC2 evidence must stay intact during migration.
- Ops: minimal change to request routing during business hours.
- Cost: target <= 10% increase YoY after negotiation.

Can each of you weigh in with a short risk/ops/procurement note by EOD Friday? I want to fold recommendations into the exec ask next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: CF_enterprise_quote_Q4_2025.pdf]

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare renewal — need options + risk notes

Marissa —

Thanks for the flag. Quick procurement read:

- Cloudflare: Current contract auto-renews Nov 30. We have a 30-day notice window for price disputes but no automatic right to terminate without penalty. Their new quote includes a 2-year term discount, but only if we commit to annual billing.
- Akamai: Ruben is offering a 12-month opt-in with a 45-day SL term; his term sheet (Akamai_term_sheet_Nov2025.pdf) includes a migration credit if we move >50% traffic within 90 days. Pricing is slightly higher but negotiable for committed volume.
- Fastly: Cassidy proposed a PoC SOW (Fastly_poc_sow.docx) — 6-week engagement, limited to two API ingress points. Upfront engineering time estimate: ~2.5 FTE-weeks.

Budget/PO notes: procurement can issue a short-term PO to bridge if we need more time to evaluate; we should avoid a lapsed WAF coverage window. If we plan a PoC, request $30k Opex for the engagement + migration support.

Recommendation: Negotiate Cloudflare aggressively (ask for a cap on price increases, SLA credits, and a migration credit). Parallel: greenlight Fastly PoC for controlled testing; keep Akamai as fallback for enterprise SLA needs.

I'll loop Legal if we decide to sign anything non-standard.

- Dev
Procurement Manager
[Attachment: Akamai_term_sheet_Nov2025.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare renewal — need options + risk notes

Folks,

From an engineering/infra perspective:

- Performance: Cloudflare has been consistent on global tail latency. Any migration risks introducing higher p95 for EU/APAC users unless we validate POP routing.
- Features: We rely on several Cloudflare managed features (WAF managed rules, Bot management, and Workers for edge auth). Fastly covers CDN + edge compute but we will need feature parity checks for our auth flows.
- KV/Cache invalidation: our purge patterns are heavy during deploys; confirm how each vendor handles mass invalidation and API rate limits.
- Rollback plan: if we do a migration, we need a staged DNS cutover and fallback (weighted load balancing) — Ops time: ~1.5 FTE-weeks for runbook + testing.

Security note: ensure WAF rule-set mapping is validated before cutover; Tessa, can you confirm whether our current SOC2 artifact package is portable or Cloudflare-specific?

My preference: Run Fastly PoC for 6 weeks to validate latency and purge behavior while we negotiate with Cloudflare. If PoC fails on features, Akamai seems the safe enterprise fallback.

— Vivek
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare renewal — need options + risk notes

Marissa / team,

Security/compliance intake: a few quick items before any vendor change:
1) SOC2 evidence portability — Cloudflare provides a cert pack that references their service boundaries. If we move to Fastly, we must confirm Fastly provides the same level of audit artifacts (SOC2 Type II) and confirm vendor subservice boundaries.
2) Data residency & logs — ensure log retention and access controls match our retention policy for audit. Akamai's term sheet mentions longer log retention for an added fee.
3) Contractual SLAs — WAF false-positive handling and emergency rule push windows must be contractually guaranteed.

Please add Security as a sign-off gate in the decision process. I can draft a short checklist for vendor comparisons.

Tessa
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@cloudflare.com>, Ruben Soto <ruben.soto@akamai.com>, Cassidy Moore <cassidy@fastly.com>, procurement@vendorops.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare renewal — need options + risk notes

Thanks all for the quick inputs — this is helpful. Summary & next steps: 

1) Negotiation: Dev to start negotiating with Cloudflare (Lena) on: a) cap on price increases, b) SLA credits for availability and WAF rule response time, c) migration credit.
2) PoC: Approve Fastly 6-week PoC limited to two APIs. Vivek to provide test plan and success criteria. PO estimate $30k — procurement to issue short-term PO if needed.
3) Akamai: Keep in parallel for enterprise-level fallback; request a revised term with a migration incentive.
4) Security: Tessa will produce a 1-page vendor-comparison checklist required for sign-off.

Attachments: CF_enterprise_quote_Q4_2025.pdf, Akamai_term_sheet_Nov2025.pdf, Fastly_poc_sow.docx

Please confirm you can execute the above by EOD Monday so I can prepare the exec slide (ask: approval to negotiate + $30k PoC budget).

Marissa
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: CF_enterprise_quote_Q4_2025.pdf]

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, procurement@vendorops.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare renewal — need options + risk notes

Confirmed — procurement will issue a $30k PO for the Fastly PoC (code: PO-RED-2025-309). I started the initial negotiation thread with Lena at Cloudflare (see CC). Ask to Lena: provide a formal counteroffer with migration credits and an SLA appendix; we'll aim to have a term sheet by Nov 21.

I'll send the PO and the draft SOW to Legal for review before any spend is finalized.

Thanks,
Dev
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PO-RED-2025-309.pdf]
